literature.headline_zh: 埃博拉病毒研究进展与应对策略。
literature.lead_zh: 近期研究聚焦于埃博拉病毒的免疫机制、疫苗研发及公共卫生应对策略,为疫情控制提供新思路。
key_findings_zh: 本迪布焦病毒(BDBV)的免疫学研究显示抗体与病毒水平存在关联,但尚未明确其临床保护效果 [10.1038/s41590-026-02623-2]。
世卫组织建议在BDBV暴发期间仅在研究方案中使用埃博拉疫苗,强调需加速开发BDBV专用疫苗 [10.2471/b09884]。
BDBV疫情中,隔离泄漏显著增加传播风险,需加强社区驱动的隔离管理 [10.64898/2026.08.25.26361360]。
非洲国家在疫情监测中面临信号整合挑战,需采用PREIS框架提升应对效率 [10.4102/jphia.v17i1.2079]。
埃博拉病毒在肝脏中引发严重损伤,与疾病严重程度和死亡率密切相关 [10.1016/j.virs.2026.08.015]。
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 埃博拉病毒疫情持续扩散,隔离泄漏和监测不足构成主要风险,需加强疫苗研发和公共卫生系统整合。
literature.caveats_zh: 部分研究基于模型或有限数据,证据强度中等,需进一步验证。
literature.headline_en: Advances in Ebola Virus Research and Response Strategies.
literature.lead_en: Recent studies focus on the immunological mechanisms, vaccine development, and public health response strategies of the Ebola virus, offering new insights for outbreak control.
key_findings_en: Immunological studies on BDBV show an association between antibody levels and viral load, but the clinical protective efficacy remains unclear [10.1038/s41590-026-02623-2]
WHO recommends the use of the Ebola vaccine only within research protocols during BDBV outbreaks, emphasizing the need for accelerated development of BDBV-specific vaccines [10.2471/b09884]
Isolation leakage during the BDBV outbreak significantly increased transmission risks, highlighting the need for community-driven isolation management [10.64898/2026.08.25.26361360]
Africa faces challenges in epidemic intelligence due to signal integration issues, requiring the adoption of the PREIS framework to enhance response efficiency [10.4102/jphia.v17i1.2079]
Ebola virus causes severe liver damage, closely associated with disease severity and mortality [10.1016/j.virs.2026.08.015]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The Ebola virus outbreak continues to spread, with isolation leakage and monitoring gaps posing significant risks, necessitating enhanced vaccine development and integrated public health systems.
literature.caveats_en: Some studies are based on models or limited data, resulting in moderate evidence strength, requiring further validation.
literature.brief_en: Recent research highlights the challenges in BDBV outbreak response, including vaccine efficacy, isolation leakage, and signal integration, emphasizing the need for improved public health strategies.

news.headline_zh: 埃博拉病毒类群本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期埃博拉病毒类群新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 世界卫生组织(WHO)报告刚果民主共和国爆发埃博拉本迪布焦病毒病疫情。该事件被确认为本迪布焦病毒病 暴发。 [news-53754a691dfc244a]

The outbreak involves confirmed and suspected cases of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease (BVD) in the DRC, reported by the World Health Organization (WHO). The outbreak is ongoing and confirmed with a case fatality ratio of 48 per cent and 1,200 recoveries. [news-3447acee7a98572f]
刚果民主共和国的埃博拉本迪布焦病毒病 暴发 正在引发二次生殖健康紧急情况,孕妇因恐惧和耻辱而避免接受医疗机构的护理。 [news-c7fa43dd9714a947]
该报告讨论了刚果民主共和国(特别是伊图里省)在指定的一周内对 埃博拉病毒病 暴发 的持续反应。它强调需要采取更快、更灵活的应对措施来遏制这种疾病的致命传播。 [news-092559d0bd289a8e]
42 天倒计时结束后,乌干达结束了埃博拉病毒 暴发。该事件由世界卫生组织非洲区域办事处报告,并确认为暴发结论。 [news-d29e861ece821965]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Ebola viruses news developments.
key_findings_en: The World Health Organization (WHO) reported on an epidemic of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The event is confirmed as an outbreak of Bundibugyo virus disease. [news-53754a691dfc244a]

The outbreak involves confirmed and suspected cases of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease (BVD) in the DRC, reported by the World Health Organization (WHO). The outbreak is ongoing and confirmed with a case fatality ratio of 48 per cent and 1,200 recoveries. [news-3447acee7a98572f]

The Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the DRC is causing a secondary reproductive health emergency, with pregnant women avoiding facility-based care due to fear and stigma. [news-c7fa43dd9714a947]

The report discusses the ongoing response to the Ebola virus disease outbreak in the DRC, particularly in the Ituri province, during the specified week. It highlights the need for a faster and more flexible response to curb the deadly spread of the disease. [news-092559d0bd289a8e]

Uganda ends an Ebola outbreak following the completion of a 42-day countdown. The event is reported by the WHO Regional Office for Africa, and it is confirmed as an outbreak conclusion. [news-d29e861ece821965]

news.brief_en: The World Health Organization (WHO) reported on an epidemic of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The event is confirmed as an outbreak of Bundibugyo virus disease. [news-53754a691dfc244a] The outbreak involves confirmed and suspected cases of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease (BVD) in the DRC, reported by the World Health Organization (WHO). The outbreak is ongoing and confirmed with a case fatality ratio of 48 per cent and 1,200 recoveries. [news-3447acee7a98572f] The Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the DRC is causing a secondary reproductive health emergency, with pregnant women avoiding facility-based care due to fear and stigma. [news-c7fa43dd9714a947] The report discusses the ongoing response to the Ebola virus disease outbreak in the DRC, particularly in the Ituri province, during the specified week. It highlights the need for a faster and more flexible response to curb the deadly spread of the disease. [news-092559d0bd289a8e] Uganda ends an Ebola outbreak following the completion of a 42-day countdown. The event is reported by the WHO Regional Office for Africa, and it is confirmed as an outbreak conclusion. [news-d29e861ece821965]

papers.title: Operational epidemiology of the early phase of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda
papers.abstract: The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda occurred in a fragile cross-border setting marked by delayed recognition, diagnostic uncertainty, insecurity, population mobility, community mistrust, and healthcare-worker exposure. We conducted a retrospective operational epidemiology study using official situation reports, public health declarations, ministry statements, WHO and Africa CDC updates, cross-border communiqués, and selected partner statements. This analysis reflects publicly available data from the early outbreak period, with the primary DRC data lock on 27 May 2026 and Uganda and regional triangulation through 29 May 2026. We reconstructed the early timeline, described epidemiological and geographic progression, quantified response indicators, and applied a transparent health-zone prioritization framework. The earliest documented symptom onset was 24 April 2026. The Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale (INRB) detected non-Zaire ebolavirus in eight of 13 samples on 14 May, giving a 20-day symptom-onset-to-first-laboratory-detection interval; species-level Bundibugyo virus confirmation and official declaration followed on 15 May. By the DRC data lock on 27 May, 125 confirmed cases and 17 confirmed deaths had been reported, giving a confirmed case fatality ratio of 13.6%. DRC also reported 906 suspected cases and 223 suspected deaths, giving a suspected fatality proportion of 24.6%. Confirmed cases expanded from three to 13 health zones across three provinces within 12 days. Ituri province accounted for 110 confirmed cases (88.0%); Bunia, Rwampara, and Mongbwalu health zones together contributed 90 cases (72.0%). Uganda reported nine confirmed cases and one death by 29 May. Operational pressure included 2,635 listed contacts in DRC, 436 contacts under follow-up in Uganda, and 126 of 774 collected samples (16.3%) pending testing in DRC. Healthcare workers represented 16 of 125 DRC confirmed cases (12.8%) and at least three of nine Uganda cases (33.3%). Applying the health-zone prioritization framework, Rwampara, Mongbwalu, and Bunia were classified as higher priority health zones. Excluding confirmed burden did not change any health-zone tier; data classification confidence was high for 10 zones and moderate for three. Within this early operational snapshot, outbreak visibility reflected both transmission and operational factors, particularly detection delay, laboratory backlog, cross-border movement, healthcare-linked exposure, and community trust or security incidents. The framework provides a transparent basis for rapid decision support during an outbreak’s early phase by directing surveillance, laboratory, case-management, infection prevention and control, contact-tracing, and community-engagement resources toward health zones where multiple operational risks converge.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the operational epidemiology of the early phase of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda. It highlights the challenges of delayed recognition, diagnostic uncertainty, and community mistrust in a fragile cross-border setting. The authors conducted a retrospective analysis using official reports and applied a health-zone prioritization framework to guide outbreak response. By 27 May 2026, 125 confirmed cases and 17 confirmed deaths were reported, with a confirmed case fatality ratio of 13.6%. Suspected cases and deaths were also documented, with a suspected fatality proportion of 24.6%. The framework was interpreted as a novel method for directing resources to high-risk health zones, particularly those with operational challenges like detection delay and healthcare-linked exposure. The study's findings have significant implications for improving surveillance and response strategies during the early stages of outbreaks. However, the reliance on publicly available data and the moderate confidence in some classifications limit the strength of the evidence.

papers.abstract_zh: 刚果民主共和国 (DRC) 和乌干达的 2026 年本迪布焦病毒病 暴发 发生在脆弱的跨境环境中,其特点是识别延迟、诊断不确定、不安全、人口流动、社区不信任和医护人员暴露。我们利用官方情况报告、公共卫生声明、部委声明、世卫组织和非洲疾病预防控制中心的最新情况、跨境公报和选定的合作伙伴声明,进行了一项回顾性操作 流行病学 研究。该分析反映了 暴发 早期的公开数据,刚果民主共和国的主要数据锁定于 2026 年 5 月 27 日,乌干达数据锁定至 2026 年 5 月 29 日。我们重建了早期时间表,描述了流行病学和地理进展,量化了应对指标,并应用了透明的卫生区优先顺序框架。最早记录的症状发作是在 2026 年 4 月 24 日。国家生物医学研究所 (INRB) 于 5 月 14 日在 13 个样本中的 8 个样本中检测到非扎伊尔埃博拉病毒,给出了从症状发作到首次实验室检测的间隔时间为 20 天;5 月 15 日,物种级本迪布焦病毒得到确认并正式宣布。截至5月27日刚果民主共和国数据锁定,已报告确诊病例125例,确诊死亡17例,确诊病死率为13.6%。刚果民主共和国还报告了 906 例疑似病例和 223 例疑似死亡,疑似死亡比例为 24.6%。12 天内,确诊病例从三个省份的 3 个卫生区扩大到 13 个。伊图里省确诊病例110例(88.0%);布尼亚、鲁万帕拉和蒙布瓦卢卫生区共报告了 90 例病例(72.0%)。截至 5 月 29 日,乌干达报告了 9 例确诊病例和 1 例死亡。运营压力包括刚果民主共和国列出的 2,635 名接触者、乌干达正在追踪的 436 名接触者以及刚果民主共和国待测试的 774 份采集样本中的 126 份 (16.3%)。刚果民主共和国 125 例确诊病例中,医护人员占 16 例(12.8%),乌干达 9 例确诊病例中至少有 3 例(33.3%)。应用卫生区优先顺序框架,鲁万帕拉、蒙布瓦卢和布尼亚被列为较高优先级卫生区。排除已确认的负担并没有改变任何健康区等级;10 个区域的数据分类置信度较高,3 个区域的数据分类置信度适中。在这个早期运营快照中,暴发 可见性反映了 传播 和运营因素,特别是检测延迟、实验室积压、跨境流动、医疗保健相关暴露以及社区信任或安全事件。该框架通过将 暴发、实验室、病例管理、感染预防和控制、接触者追踪和社区参与资源引导到多个运营风险集中的卫生区,为 暴发 早期阶段的快速决策支持提供透明的基础。

papers.title: Liver injury during Ebola virus infections: Characteristics and molecular mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Ebola virus (EBOV) causes severe and often fatal Ebola virus disease (EVD) in humans, posing a major threat to global public health. Since EVD was first identified in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) in 1976, the World Health Organization (WHO) has declared it a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) on three occasions. EBOV infection is characterized by rapid progression from non-specific febrile illness to severe gastrointestinal symptoms, followed by hemorrhagic fever and multi-organ dysfunction, with case fatality rates reaching as high as 90%. The liver is a primary target of EBOV, and virus-induced liver injury is characterized by elevated aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels, mild hyperbilirubinemia, impaired coagulation factor synthesis, hepatocyte necrosis, and robust inflammatory responses, all of which are closely correlated with disease severity and mortality risk. In this review, we summarize the characteristics and mechanisms of EBOV-induced liver injury, which may help to further elucidate the pathogenesis of EVD and provide novel strategies for combating EBOV infection.

papers.full_text: In the context of a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, such as the Bundibugyo virus outbreak, the research community requires rapid access to information to guide an effective response. Evidence mapping brings together the available knowledge in a field into a single, organized resource, enabling researchers to rapidly identify priorities, gaps and opportunities for action. Subjects Immunology and microbiology research is crucial for combatting emerging infectious diseases. This was demonstrated during the COVID-19 pandemic when multiple vaccines, monoclonal antibody treatments and diagnostics were rapidly developed. The recent World Health Organization declaration of the Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) signals the need for researchers to once again respond dynamically to address a major health crisis. A challenge for immunologists in pivoting their research to a new area is knowing what has already been studied, and what the priorities are. Determining this requires investigators to have an overview of the literature in the new field and to be confident that they have not missed a crucial study that might affect the direction or usefulness of their research. For individual investigators, this first step of gaining an overview of the literature in a new field can require a substantial investment of time and act as a barrier to entry. But what if all the relevant literature on the topic had already been assembled and categorized? Evidence mapping aims to provide exactly that resource, enabling researchers to quickly find all the published research that is relevant to their work. Evidence mapping of filovirus research Evidence mapping is a systematic process for identifying relevant publications in a specific area and categorizing them according to the evidence they provide (Fig. 1). The identified literature is then displayed as a two-dimensional map categorized according to population (for example, human, non-human primate (NHP), mouse), intervention (for example, vaccination, infection, treatment) and the outcomes measured (for example, antibody response, T cell response, outcome of infection). In contrast to traditional narrative literature reviews, an evidence map is specifically designed to provide a comprehensive and unbiased assembly of the available research, enabling researchers to conduct their own downstream analyses. The screening and mapping are performed independently by two reviewers to help ensure consistency, and the resulting maps can be disseminated as a resource for the wider research community. Maps can also be made ‘living’ by regular updates to keep them current. In 2024, the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI) identified the benefits of assembling the existing evidence on immunity and vaccination for their priority pathogens and providing this as an open resource for the health and medical communities. CEPI commissioned the development of evidence maps for three filoviruses, Marburg virus (MARV), Sudan virus (SUDV) and Ebola virus (EBOV), which were first produced in early 2025 and updated in September 2025. When the BDBV PHEIC was declared on 17 May 2026, the mapping team rapidly assembled to make a map of the available evidence on BDBV vaccination and immunity. The resulting map was posted online on 21 May 2026 and updated on 22 July 2026 (available at https://livingevidence.org.au/research-initiatives/about-feeva/evidence-maps/), and a preprint1 of the methods was published on 24 May 2026. Rapid production of an evidence map for BDBV was possible because of the established method for mapping filoviruses2 and the fact that only a small number of studies on BDBV immunity were available. A total of 49 publications were included on the original map (with an additional eight included in subsequent updates). By contrast, the equivalent maps for EBOV, MARV and SUDV include 857, 198 and 147 publications, respectively. Immunological findings for BDBV Immunity to filoviruses is thought to be largely mediated through antibodies to the surface glycoprotein. Two vaccines for EBOV have been approved, both based on the EBOV glycoprotein. Unfortunately, early evidence indicates limited cross-reactivity between the EBOV and BDBV glycoproteins, and it remains unclear whether EBOV vaccines will be effective against BDBV3. A number of animal studies have shown that BDBV glycoprotein-based vaccines and monoclonal antibodies to the BDBV glycoprotein can protect from severe infection4,5. Animal models of vaccination and infection were central to the approval of the Zabdeno/Mvabea vaccine for EBOV. These studies demonstrated that vaccine-induced antibody levels were associated with protection in a NHP model of EBOV infection6. By comparing the protective antibody levels in NHPs and the antibody levels induced after human vaccination, the investigators predicted that Zabdeno/Mvabea would be protective against EBOV infection in humans. Could a similar immunobridging approach be used in BDBV? Numerous animal models have been used for BDBV (including NHPs, mice, ferrets, pigs). However, only four studies have looked at the association between vaccine-induced antibody levels and protection from infection in a cynomolgus macaque model of BDBV infection. Two studies analyzed prophylactic vaccination, with one study showing an association between antibody levels and protection7 but another study showing no association8. Similarly, two studies analyzed vaccination around the time of infection. While one study of vaccination 3 or 7 days before infection showed an association between antibody levels and viral levels (in a non-peer-reviewed preprint9), another study of post-exposure prophylaxis was difficult to interpret because of the dynamic nature of early immune responses to vaccination and infection4. Further work on correlates of protection from BDBV infection in NHPs is clearly needed to support potential immunobridging. Understanding the immune response to natural BDBV infection — and whether natural immunity confers immunity to reinfection — could also inform the immune responses required for protection. However, there are only 10 studies of immune responses in survivors of BDBV (none of which measured T cell responses). In the case of EBOV, previous infection is thought to confer at least short-term immunity to reinfection (although cases of viral recrudescence have been reported; reviewed in ref. 10). However, it is not clear whether BDBV infection confers subsequent immunity to BDBV reinfection. Studies of the phenotype and durability of immune responses in survivors of BDBV infection — and whether or which of these responses confer protection from reinfection — are an important priority. Key to this is the development and dissemination of validated immunoassays for BDBV, which is critical to enable comparison of immune responses across natural history and vaccination studies, and to compare responses between animal models and human infection. Challenges and future directions While analysis of the current immunological literature on BDBV (through the evidence map) highlights the need for further characterization of immunity to BDBV, the challenges of performing such research should not be underestimated. The outbreak itself is occurring in a resource-limited setting affected by conflict. BDBV is highly pathogenic, meaning it must usually be handled in biosafety level 4 facilities, greatly reducing the number of laboratories that can perform such studies. However, the challenge of BDBV research also highlights the importance of using robust, validated and, ideally, standardized assays in those studies that are performed. Further, these studies should focus on the key gaps in BDBV knowledge that are most important for the public health response and for the development of vaccines and therapeutics. Comparison with the work on EBOV, SUDV and MARV gives a useful perspective on what is possible. Evidence mapping provides a novel approach to support the research community, accelerating research to resolve the current BDBV outbreak and providing a key tool to support research on future health threats. analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the need for rapid access to information during a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, such as the Bundibugyo virus outbreak, by creating an evidence map of relevant literature on vaccination and immunity. The map was assembled quickly following the WHO's declaration of the BDBV outbreak as a PHEIC on 17 May 2026, and it serves as a dynamic resource for researchers. The evidence mapping process involved systematic identification and categorization of publications, with two independent reviewers ensuring consistency. The results highlight the importance of evidence mapping in guiding research priorities and improving preparedness for emerging infectious diseases. The study's limitations include the potential exclusion of recent studies, but the use of independent reviewers and regular updates enhances the reliability of the findings. The evidence is considered moderate in strength, as it relies on existing literature rather than original data.

papers.title: Nurses’ Lived Experiences of Caring for Patients During the 2022 Ebola Virus Disease Outbreak in Uganda: A Qualitative Study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Nurses play a pivotal role during infectious disease outbreaks, including Ebola Virus Disease (EVD), often placing themselves at significant personal and professional risk. While nurses are central to Ebola response efforts, their lived experiences, particularly in Uganda, remain underexplored. This study aimed to explore the lived experiences of nurses who provided care to EVD patients during the 2022 outbreak at Mubende Regional Referral Hospital. Methods An exploratory qualitative design was employed using in-depth interviews with seven nurses who worked in the Ebola Treatment Unit (ETU). Participants were selected through purposive and snowball sampling. Data were analysed thematically using a phenomenological approach to capture the emotional, psychological, and professional dimensions of nurses’ experiences. Results Findings revealed a complex interplay of positive and negative experiences. Positive experiences included joy from patient recovery, strong teamwork, professional growth, and enhanced training in infection prevention and control (IPC). Nurses reported increased confidence, new skills, and opportunities for career advancement, including recognition from international agencies. Conversely, negative experiences dominated the narratives. These included severe resource constraints, overwhelming workload, physical exhaustion, and psychological distress, particularly from witnessing patient suffering and death. Participants described post-traumatic stress symptoms and constant fear of infection and death, exacerbated by inadequate early-stage preparation. Social isolation and disrupted family life were also common, with some nurses concealing their work to avoid distressing loved ones or experiencing stigma within their communities. Additional challenges included team tensions, absenteeism, and disparities in compensation and recognition between existing staff and external recruits. Conclusion The study highlights the profound emotional and professional toll on nurses during the 2022 Ebola outbreak in Uganda. While moments of resilience and growth were evident, structural and systemic challenges significantly impacted nurses’ well-being and care delivery. To better support frontline health workers, future outbreak responses must prioritize fair compensation, psychosocial support, consistent training, and improved resource allocation. Insights from this study can inform policies aimed at strengthening workforce readiness and retention during health emergencies.

papers.title: Epidemiology of Sudan Ebolavirus Disease Cases in Uganda, January-April, 2025.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: On January 30, 2025, the Ministry of Health, Uganda (MoH), announced an outbreak of Sudan ebolavirus disease (SVD). We describe the epidemiological characteristics and transmission dynamics of the SVD outbreak in Uganda during January-April, 2025. METHODS: SVD cases were identified using MoH case definitions and were classified as confirmed if positive on RT-qPCR or probable if an SVD-related death was reported with epidemiological linkage but without laboratory confirmation. analysis_zh.main_results: 2025年1月30日至4月25日期间发现了14例病例:12例(86%)为确诊病例,2例(14%)为疑似病例;5 名(36%)是卫生工作者。4 例死亡,病死率 (CFR) 为 29% (4/14)。大多数暴露是家庭暴露(9[64%]),其次是医疗保健相关暴露(3[21%])。共监控534名接触者;其中 454 人(85%)被隔离。已知接触者中没有发生二次 传播。估计的 Rt(四分位数间距)为 1.1 (0.83-1.35)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解释为表明病死率和有效再生数较低,这可能是由于早期发现、迅速识别、隔离和密切监测接触者所致。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为 监测 和苏丹埃博拉病毒病的控制策略提供信息,强调早期检测和接触者追踪在缓解 暴发 方面的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据受到对报告病例和接触者监测的依赖的限制,没有提供详细的统计分析或模型。由于该研究的观察性质,对研究结果的可信度中等。

papers.title: Ebola Virus Disease in the Era of One Health and Global Preparedness: Evolving Epidemiology, Genomic Surveillance, and Future Challenges
papers.abstract: Ebola virus disease (EVD) remains one of the most severe viral hemorrhagic fevers, with recurrent outbreaks challenging global healthcare systems. This narrative review traces the evolving epidemiology of EVD from the first recognized outbreaks in 1976 to the ongoing 2026 Bundibugyo virus public health emergency in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda. Over nearly five decades, the recognized range of Ebola outbreak contexts and amplification mechanisms has broadened considerably: rural zoonotic spillovers remain the predominant mode of emergence, but the scale and reach of subsequent transmission increasingly depend on where introductions occur, on delays in detection, on population mobility, on ecological disruption, on armed conflict, on healthcare-associated transmission, and on viral persistence in survivors. Major advances in molecular epidemiology and genomic surveillance have improved outbreak investigation, enabling real-time transmission reconstruction and detection of survivor-linked resurgence. Vaccination, particularly ring vaccination with rVSV-ZEBOV, has shown high effectiveness against Zaire ebolavirus, yet vaccine equity gaps and the absence of licensed vaccines for Sudan virus and Bundibugyo virus remain critical vulnerabilities, though new candidate vaccines and therapeutics for Bundibugyo virus entered clinical evaluation in mid-2026. Artificial intelligence and digital technologies, including AI-assisted early warning systems, portable sequencing, drones, blockchain, and mobile health platforms, offer promising tools for outbreak preparedness, but robust evidence of their real-world operational impact during filovirus outbreaks remains limited, and their deployment in low-resource settings faces substantial barriers related to infrastructure, literacy, data costs, and governance. Integrated preparedness frameworks that combine ecological surveillance, resilient healthcare systems, community engagement, and international coordination under a One Health umbrella are increasingly viewed as a strategic necessity. The 2026 Bundibugyo outbreak reaffirms that despite decades of lessons, structural weaknesses in surveillance, response timeliness, and community trust continue to recur. Sustainable, multi-year financing, diversified vaccine platforms, regional manufacturing, and local co-design of digital tools are essential to translate lessons into lasting change. Preparedness is best understood as a continuous process rather than a reactive state.

papers.abstract_zh: 埃博拉病毒病 (EVD) 仍然是最严重的病毒性出血热之一,反复发作的 暴发 对全球医疗保健系统构成挑战。这篇叙述性回顾追溯了埃博拉病毒病 流行病学 的演变过程,从 1976 年首次公认的 暴发 到 2026 年刚果民主共和国 (DRC) 和乌干达持续发生的本迪布焦病毒公共卫生紧急情况。近五年来,埃博拉 暴发 背景和放大机制的公认范围已大大扩大:农村人畜共患 传播 仍然是主要的出现方式,但随后 传播 的规模和影响范围越来越多地取决于引入发生的地点、检测延迟、人口流动性、生态破坏、武装冲突、与医疗保健相关的 传播 以及幸存者中病毒的持续存在。分子 流行病学 和 基因组监测 的重大进展改进了 暴发 调查,实现了实时 传播 重建和幸存者相关复苏的检测。疫苗接种,特别是带有 rVSV-ZEBOV 的 环形疫苗接种,已显示出对抗扎伊尔埃博拉病毒的高效性,但 疫苗 的股权差距以及缺乏针对苏丹病毒和本迪布焦病毒的 疫苗 许可仍然是严重的漏洞,尽管新的候选药物 疫苗 和本迪布焦病毒的治疗方法已于 2026 年中期进入临床评估。人工智能和数字技术,包括人工智能辅助早期预警系统、便携式测序、无人机、区块链和移动医疗平台,为暴发的防备提供了有前景的工具,但其在丝状病毒暴发期间的实际操作影响的有力证据仍然有限,而且它们在资源匮乏的环境中的部署面临着与基础设施、读写能力、数据成本和治理相关的巨大障碍。综合准备框架将生态 监测、弹性医疗保健系统、社区参与和“同一个健康”保护伞下的国际协调结合起来,越来越被视为战略必要性。2026 年 Bundibugyo 暴发 重申,尽管有数十年的经验教训,但 监测 、响应及时性和社区信任方面的结构性弱点仍在继续出现。可持续的多年融资、多元化的 疫苗 平台、区域制造以及数字工具的本地协同设计对于将经验教训转化为持久变革至关重要。准备工作最好理解为一个持续的过程,而不是一种反应状态。

analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 近五年来,埃博拉 暴发 背景和放大机制的公认范围已大大扩大:农村人畜共患 传播 仍然是主要的出现方式,但随后 传播 的规模和影响范围越来越多地取决于引入发生的地点、检测延迟、人口流动性、生态破坏、武装冲突、与医疗保健相关的 传播 以及幸存者中病毒的持续存在。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 分子 流行病学 和 基因组监测 的重大进展改进了 暴发 调查,实现了实时 传播 重建和幸存者相关复苏的检测。2026 年 Bundibugyo 暴发 重申,尽管有数十年的经验教训,但 监测 、响应及时性和社区信任方面的结构性弱点仍在继续出现。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 可持续的多年融资、多元化的 疫苗 平台、区域制造以及数字工具的本地协同设计对于将经验教训转化为持久变革至关重要。准备工作最好理解为一个持续的过程,而不是一种反应状态。

papers.title: Aligning Licensure and Recommended Use to Expedite Vaccine Access in Response to the Ongoing Bundibugyo Ebolavirus Epidemic in Central Africa
papers.abstract: The ongoing Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense—Bundibugyo virus (BDBV)—epidemic is the worst Ebolavirus outbreak in a decade and is rapidly expanding, with >4600 suspected cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) alone. It has caused 2186 deaths and spread to neighboring countries. As BDBV has no approved vaccine, timely response will require adapted use of existing vaccines approved for other ebolaviruses and expedited development of novel vaccines targeted toward BDBV. Access to vaccines is fundamental to public health emergency response and generally depends on two expert bodies in each country: a national regulatory authority (e.g., the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)) and a national immunization advisor. Receding traditional global health assistance compounds already-limited licensure and recommended use in the DRC and other low-income countries confronting recent outbreaks of Ebola, Marburg, and mpox, exacerbating access gaps for high-risk populations. This commentary thus clarifies the critical importance of a robust national immunization advisor, coordinated closely with expanded licensure, in expediting access to vaccines and other essential epidemic response tools. Using the regulatory responses of the Republic of Rwanda and DRC, it demonstrates that clearer delineation of roles between these bodies is critical for effective response, can help prioritize self-sufficiency and greater regional public health cooperation, and will thus enable swifter control of Bundibugyo.

The findings underscore the necessity of coordinated regulatory actions to expedite vaccine availability, which has implications for improving emergency preparedness. However, the study is based on a commentary and lacks empirical data, limiting its evidence strength to a moderate level.

papers.title: “They could ...distance themselves from me claiming I still had Ebola”: experiences of Ebola virus disease survivors in Central Uganda
papers.abstract: Ebola continues to be a great public health challenge in Uganda where it is vulnerable to future Ebola outbreaks. Survivors are likely to continue experiencing the after effects of Ebola during the recovery period. The study was conducted to explore experiences of Ebola survivors during and after the recovery period. A descriptive qualitative study was conducted in central Uganda. Thematic deductive analysis was applied to analyze the data. Participants had varied response to Ebola diagnosis. Participants were initially hesitant to seek care, but they eventually agreed with their Ebola diagnosis and complied with medical treatment. Ebola survivors had conspiracy theories regarding Ebola which persisted even after survival. Ebola was attributed to witchcraft, while others thought it was introduced to reduce their population size and as a vehicle for organ donation. Survival was attributed to trade-offs with government and pretense of being sick. Ebola patients and survivors had formal and informal support from government and non-governmental organization which helped meet their social, physical and emotional needs during and after admission. Ebola patients and survivors had emotional, social, and physical challenges during admission and after discharge. Ebola patients experienced enormous emotional trauma related to worries of survival. Emotional and physical challenges persisted after discharge and they emanated from stigma, discrimination, financial constraints, marital problems and persisting physical ailments. Ensuring patients understand and adopt coping mechanisms reduces this stigma. There is need for community-based mental health and psychosocial interventions integrated within a broader package of care for EVD survivors.

papers.title: Signal integration challenges in African epidemic intelligence: Lessons from the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak and application of the PREIS framework
papers.abstract: On 17 May 2026, the Director-General of the World Health Organization determined that Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda constituted a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. Ten days separated the initial alert (05 May) from laboratory confirmation (15 May) although multiple non-laboratory signals were already active. Using this outbreak, we argue that Africa’s principal detection challenge is often not signal availability but the timely interpretive integration of concurrent multi-source signals, and we outline how a reproducible analytical layer – the Pan-African Real-time Epidemiological Intelligence System (PREIS) framework – might support it.
papers.journal: Journal of Public Health in Africa

Ten days separated the initial alert (05 May) from laboratory confirmation (15 May) although multiple non-laboratory signals were already active. Using this outbreak, we argue that Africa’s principal detection challenge is often not signal availability but the timely interpretive integration of concurrent multi-source signals, and we outline how a reproducible analytical layer – the Pan-African Real-time Epidemiological Intelligence System (PREIS) framework – might support it.
source_records.journal: Journal of Public Health in Africa

analysis.methods: The study used the PREIS framework to develop a reproducible analytical layer for integrating signals. It emphasized the importance of timely interpretive integration of concurrent multi-source signals to improve epidemic intelligence.

papers.title: Ebola virus disease and the 2026 FIFA World Cup mass gatherings: implications for global health security
papers.abstract: The 2026 Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA) World Cup kicked off on June 11, 2026 in Mexico with the first opening match. It is unarguably the largest football event in the history of FIFA-organized tournaments, with three nations United States of America, Canada, and Mexico jointly hosting a 48-nation tournament featuring 104 matches. In contrast, previous tournaments, such as the 2022 event in Qatar, were limited to 32 participating countries and a single host nation. The number of participating countries from Africa was raised from five to nine with the epicentre of the current Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreak, DR Congo (DRC) one of the participating countries having qualified through the intercontinental play off. Equally important is the fact that it is the longest running World Cup event lasting 39 days compared to 32 days previously.
papers.journal: International Journal Of Community Medicine And Public Health

analysis.main_results: The 2026 FIFA World Cup featured nine African nations, including DRC, which had been affected by an Ebola virus disease outbreak. The event lasted 39 days, longer than the previous 32-day duration.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the increased participation of African nations, including DRC, in the World Cup could pose significant challenges for global health security due to the potential for disease transmission during large gatherings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for enhanced surveillance and preparedness measures during international mass gatherings, particularly in regions affected by Ebola virus disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its descriptive nature and lack of quantitative data on disease transmission risks. The evidence is moderate as it relies on event characteristics rather than direct health outcomes.

papers.title: Impact of Detection-Isolation-Leakage on the 2026 DRC Bundibugyo Ebolavirus Outbreak
papers.abstract: The 17th Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, announced on 15 May 2026, was attributed to Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV). Although case isolation is the main control strategy, its effectiveness is compromised when patients escape isolation facilities before recovery. Between 14 May and 17 June 2026, 175 individuals reportedly left isolation facilities without formal discharge across Ituri Province. We assessed how this "isolation leakage" affects community transmission. We refined the SEIHFR framework to distinguish undetected community infections, detected but not-yet-isolated cases, isolated individuals, leakage, funeral-associated transmission, and removals. Using Bayesian inference, we fitted the model to daily Ituri surveillance data, escapee counts, and isolation census records. We estimated the leakage rate, reporting and detection probabilities, and the transmission rate, while fixing other parameters based on the BDBV literature. The model reproduced confirmed cases, deaths, discharges, and escapees. We estimated R_0=3.67 (95% HDI: 2.0-5.7), a leakage rate of {rho} {approx} 0.034 day^-1 (0.022-0.051), and high contact-tracing-driven detection (p_d {approx} 0.91-0.99). Leakage increased the detection-dependent reproduction number [R](p_d) from approximately 3.2 to above 5. Eliminating leakage reduced cumulative infections by about one-third, from 1,120 to 764, while the minimum detection level required for control increased from p_d [≥] 0.73 without leakage to p_d [≥] 0.87 at the fitted leakage rate. Shortening time to isolation prevented the most infections (73.4%; 59-84), followed by reducing leakage (29.7%; 14-52) and re-isolating escapees (12.6%; 6-24). Delaying leakage reduction until week 4 reduced its benefit from about 27% to below 2%. Isolation leakage represents a major transmission pathway that has until now gone largely unmeasured. While rapid initiation of isolation is highly beneficial, it cannot compensate for permeable isolation; therefore, early, community-driven efforts to control leakage, embedded within a multilayered response, are critical.

Introduction The ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), which was recently declared over in Uganda, underscores persistent challenges of preparedness and response to Ebola in complex social, political, and economic environments. Despite medical advances [1] outbreaks recur, exposing critical gaps in the entire mitigation continuum. Effective outbreak response requires multi-level, multidisciplinary collaboration spanning local, national, and international actors. Collaboration with local communities is key for effective outbreak response. While Uganda has been successful in containing the present and previous Ebola outbreaks, our research shows that disease outbreak management remains dominated by a top-down response logic. Our ongoing work on Ebola outbreak response in western and central Uganda shows how this leads to a lack of trust in government-led interventions and, by extension, to suboptimal compliance. Previous research has reported similar findings from DRC [2–5]. During the current outbreak, as during previous ones, local communities in Uganda and DRC have been documented to label Ebola outbreaks as made up by the government based on hidden agendas. Research shows that, across contexts and diseases, lack of compliance with public health interventions is often connected with lack of trust in authorities [2,4]. These kinds of suspicions lead to dismissal of risks and disregard of mitigation efforts. In our work in western and central Uganda, Ebola outbreaks have been described as distractions to facilitate government interests, such as control over mining areas or suppression of political opposition. These narratives highlight the importance of trust in governing institutions for successful outbreak response and the limitations of short-sighted and top-down risk communication strategies. Community engagement must build on transparency and trust, and a deeper understanding of livelihood struggles in Ebola-prone settings [2]. Another reason for non-compliance is that local communities perceive that government recommendations on avoiding certain livelihood activities are unrealistic, as alternative livelihood options are not available or not seen as viable [2]. One example is how cross-border trade in bush meat between the DRC and Uganda persists despite repeated warnings about its association with Ebola outbreaks [2]. This underscores the need to adapt outbreak preparedness in dialogue with local communities, not only to ensure trust with authorities, but also to avoid undermining essential livelihood practices. Mitigation strategies should extend beyond emergency medical responses to encompass two-way dialogue with communities to ensure that Ebola response measures are locally understood and trusted, and do not undermine local livelihoods. Ebola virus transmission impacted by healthcare- and community dynamics As expected for an emerging disease, there will be a delay between the index case and the identification of an outbreak. Additionally, high endemic occurrence of differential diagnoses such as malaria, lack of routines to prevent nosocomial infection transmission, and insufficient appreciation of how traditional practices and belief systems shape local responses often lead to misinterpretation or delayed recognition of Ebola symptoms, as observed in the current outbreak. During the time between outbreak and detection, the disease spreads within communities, exposing the public and healthcare workers to risk of infection. The current outbreak in Uganda exemplifies this pattern, having been identified following the burial of a Congolese national who had sought care in Uganda, leading to virus exposure and infection among unsuspecting healthcare workers [6]. Transmission pathways remain consistent across outbreaks, frequently involving avoidable practices such as unprotected contacts between febrile patients and healthcare workers, traditional burials, and resistance to medical isolation [7]. Communities are therefore both the epicentre of transmission and the key to early containment. However, complacency with public health interventions persists [5]. Recent and ongoing events—including escape from Ebola treatment units and attacks on response infrastructure in parts of the DRC—demonstrate that communities have not been sufficiently engaged in preventive initiatives. Past successes demonstrate the importance of inclusive community involvement. The 2014–2016 West Africa Ebola outbreak showed that effective containment required thoughtful long-term engagement with local populations [8]. Contemporary context: Uganda and the DRC Uganda and the DRC continue to dominate the landscape of Ebola outbreaks in Africa. The DRC remains affected by prolonged civil unrest and inequality, resulting in widespread poverty, displacement, and fragile health systems [9]. Similarly, the fatal 2000–2001 Ebola outbreak in northern Uganda occurred under conditions of civil unrest. Civil unrest and political instability breed poverty, weaken health systems, and drain public trust. In addition, insecurity limits access to affected populations [10]. Uganda shares borders with the DRC, and regular cross-border movement of people and goods contributes to outbreak spillovers, including in the present outbreak. Consequently, some Ugandans perceive Ebola as an external threat, reducing perceived personal risk and weakening preventive behaviours. Our findings suggest that the epidemiology and disease impact of Ebola are affected by structural challenges such as poverty, weak governance, and inadequate healthcare systems. In many cases, recurrent Ebola outbreaks are less the primary problem than a symptom of broader systemic inequities [11]. Poverty drives high-risk behaviours such as bushmeat consumption and disregarding public health interventions for survival reasons. Both Uganda and the DRC also face outbreak governance challenges, including reliance on external funding and limited domestic capacity for outbreak response [12]. Whereas Uganda has shown significant capacities in disease outbreak management [13], its top-down approach to response has impacted how citizens perceive disease outbreaks. The ongoing outbreak clearly demonstrates how weak governance systems can drive outbreaks in unpredictable directions, leading to avoidable mortality and further erosion of public trust. Call to action Addressing Ebola outbreaks sustainably requires comprehensive preparedness and response strategies that account for the social, political, and economic determinants of health. The ongoing outbreak is a critical reminder that efforts must extend beyond emergency response to address underlying inequalities, strengthen local health systems, and build public trust. Key priorities include institutionalizing community engagement to foster transparency and integrating preparedness into routine service delivery. There is also a need to reframe how socio-cultural practices are labelled in outbreak contexts [14]. Portraying local traditions, livelihoods, and domestic environments as inherently pathogenic risks undermines community dignity and weakens engagement efforts. A more constructive approach involves recognizing and integrating local knowledge systems, addressing structural inequalities, and fostering genuine partnerships between communities and health governance institutions. Only through such holistic and sustained efforts can meaningful preparedness, response, and long-term prevention of Ebola outbreaks—including the current one—be achieved as illustrated in Fig 1 below. papers.title_original: Beyond Ebola disease: The role of government-citizen relationship in shaping Community outbreak behavior and outcomes

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore how government-citizen relationships influence community behavior and outcomes during Ebola outbreaks, highlighting the need to address trust issues in public health interventions. The ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), recently declared over in Uganda, underscores persistent challenges in outbreak preparedness and response in complex social, political, and economic environments.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is based on field observations conducted within the project "Community Engagement for Improved Ebola Disease Outbreak Prevention and Response in Uganda - Co-design for Future Global and Local Strategies". It focuses on local communities in Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) during Ebola outbreaks, examining how trust in government-led interventions affects compliance with public health measures.
analysis.methods: The study utilized field observations and qualitative data from community interactions during Ebola outbreaks in Uganda and DRC. It analyzed how government-citizen relationships shaped community perceptions of risk and compliance with outbreak response strategies.
analysis.main_results: The study found that local communities in Uganda and DRC have labeled Ebola outbreaks as being made up by the government based on hidden agendas. This suspicion leads to dismissal of risks and disregard of mitigation efforts, resulting in suboptimal compliance with public health interventions.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as evidence that trust in government is critical for effective outbreak response, and they highlight the novelty of linking outbreak outcomes to the dynamics of government-citizen relationships rather than solely to medical or epidemiological factors.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for improved community engagement and trust-building strategies in public health interventions, particularly for Ebola virus disease. They emphasize the importance of understanding social and political contexts in outbreak management to enhance compliance and improve outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on observational data and qualitative analysis, which may introduce bias and limit the generalizability of findings. However, the evidence is supported by field studies and aligns with previous research on similar themes, providing a moderate level of confidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines how government-citizen relationships influence community behavior and outcomes during Ebola outbreaks in Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). It highlights that distrust in government-led interventions leads to suboptimal compliance with public health measures, as communities often suspect hidden agendas behind outbreak declarations. The research underscores the importance of trust in effective outbreak response and suggests that social and political dynamics must be considered alongside medical and epidemiological factors. While the study is based on observational data and qualitative analysis, it aligns with previous findings and provides a moderate level of confidence in its conclusions. The implications for public health emphasize the need for improved community engagement and trust-building strategies to enhance outbreak management and improve outcomes.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在探讨埃博拉 暴发 期间政府与公民关系如何影响社区行为和结果,强调需要解决公共卫生干预措施中的信任问题。刚果民主共和国 (DRC) 正在爆发的埃博拉病毒 暴发 最近在乌干达宣布结束,突显出在复杂的社会、政治和经济环境中,暴发 的准备和应对工作面临着持续的挑战。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究基于“社区参与改善乌干达埃博拉疾病 暴发 预防和应对 - 共同设计未来全球和地方战略”项目中进行的实地观察。它重点关注埃博拉 暴发 期间乌干达和刚果民主共和国 (DRC) 的当地社区,研究对政府主导干预措施的信任如何影响公共卫生措施的遵守情况。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究利用了乌干达和刚果民主共和国埃博拉 暴发 期间社区互动的实地观察和定性数据。它分析了政府与公民的关系如何影响社区对风险的认知以及对 暴发 应对策略的遵守情况。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究发现,乌干达和刚果民主共和国的当地社区将埃博拉病毒贴上了“暴发”的标签,称其是政府根据隐藏议程捏造的。这种怀疑导致忽视风险和忽视缓解措施,导致公共卫生干预措施的遵守情况不佳。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明对政府的信任对于有效的 暴发 应对至关重要,他们强调了将 暴发 结果与政府与公民关系的动态联系起来的新颖性,而不仅仅是与医学或流行病学因素联系起来。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore how government-citizen relationships influence community behavior and outcomes during Ebola outbreaks, highlighting the need to address trust issues in public health interventions. The ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), recently declared over in Uganda, underscores persistent challenges in outbreak preparedness and response in complex social, political, and economic environments.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study is based on field observations conducted within the project "Community Engagement for Improved Ebola Disease Outbreak Prevention and Response in Uganda - Co-design for Future Global and Local Strategies". It focuses on local communities in Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) during Ebola outbreaks, examining how trust in government-led interventions affects compliance with public health measures.
analysis_en.methods: The study utilized field observations and qualitative data from community interactions during Ebola outbreaks in Uganda and DRC. It analyzed how government-citizen relationships shaped community perceptions of risk and compliance with outbreak response strategies.
analysis_en.main_results: The study found that local communities in Uganda and DRC have labeled Ebola outbreaks as being made up by the government based on hidden agendas. This suspicion leads to dismissal of risks and disregard of mitigation efforts, resulting in suboptimal compliance with public health interventions.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as evidence that trust in government is critical for effective outbreak response, and they highlight the novelty of linking outbreak outcomes to the dynamics of government-citizen relationships rather than solely to medical or epidemiological factors.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for improved community engagement and trust-building strategies in public health interventions, particularly for Ebola virus disease. They emphasize the importance of understanding social and political contexts in outbreak management to enhance compliance and improve outcomes.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on observational data and qualitative analysis, which may introduce bias and limit the generalizability of findings. However, the evidence is supported by field studies and aligns with previous research on similar themes, providing a moderate level of confidence.

papers.title: A small molecule inhibits Ebola virus entry through glycoprotein stabilization
papers.abstract: Abstract Ebola virus (EBOV) causes outbreaks with high fatality rates, yet potent small-molecule inhibitors targeting EBOV glycoprotein (GP) remain limited. Here, using DNA-encoded chemical libraries, we screen 4.73 billion compounds against EBOV GP and, through stereochemical optimization, identify MWAC-3634. This compound binds GP with high affinity (K d =40.7 nM), potently neutralizes infection (IC50 = 0.65 nM), shows no detectable cytotoxicity, and exhibits favorable pharmacokinetics in mice. This potency substantially exceeds that of known small-molecule inhibitors targeting EBOV GP. Cryo-EM at 2.54 Å resolution reveals that MWAC-3634 occupies a hydrophobic cavity at the GP subunit interface and stabilizes GP, supporting an entry-blocking mechanism distinct from previously described GP-destabilizing inhibitors. In a lethal-challenge mouse model, MWAC-3634 administered either intraperitoneally or orally substantially improves survival and reduces clinical signs. These findings suggest that EBOV GP requires an optimal level of stability for entry, identify GP stabilization as an effective anti-filovirus strategy, and establish MWAC-3634 as a promising lead compound for development.

analysis.summary_en: This study identifies MWAC-3634, a small molecule that inhibits Ebola virus entry by stabilizing its glycoprotein. The research was motivated by the high fatality rates of Ebola virus disease and the limited availability of effective small-molecule inhibitors. The compound was discovered through screening of DNA-encoded chemical libraries and stereochemical optimization, demonstrating high affinity for EBOV GP and potent neutralization of infection. Cryo-EM analysis revealed that MWAC-3634 binds to a hydrophobic cavity at the GP subunit interface, stabilizing the protein and blocking viral entry. In a mouse model, MWAC-3634 significantly improved survival and reduced clinical signs when administered intraperitoneally or orally. The findings suggest that maintaining an optimal level of GP stability is crucial for viral entry, highlighting GP stabilization as a novel therapeutic strategy. However, the study is limited to in vitro and in vivo models, and further research is needed to confirm efficacy in humans. The evidence is strong and well-supported by the experimental data.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This guidance addresses the need for recommendations on the potential use of Ervebo® during outbreaks of Bundibugyo virus disease, considering the evolving outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and additional evidence reviewed by SAGE.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is an interim guidance document that outlines the design for a ring randomized controlled trial to generate efficacy data for Ervebo® against Bundibugyo virus, with a focus on outbreak settings and human populations.
analysis.methods: The methods involve reviewing animal, immunological and observational evidence, and emphasize the need for rapidly generating robust efficacy data through a ring randomized controlled trial, while maintaining proven outbreak-control measures.
analysis.main_results: The guidance reports that available evidence remains insufficient to determine whether Ervebo® provides clinically meaningful protection or to quantify vaccine efficacy in humans against Bundibugyo virus.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the off-label use of Ervebo® during BDBV outbreaks is associated with benefits, risks and uncertainties, and that the guidance recommends its use only within research protocols.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the cautious use of Ervebo® during BDBV outbreaks and highlight the need for accelerated development and evaluation of BDBV-specific vaccines and countermeasures.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by insufficient data on clinically meaningful protection and vaccine efficacy against BDBV, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This WHO interim guidance addresses the use of the licensed Ebola vaccine Ervebo® during outbreaks of Bundibugyo virus disease. It acknowledges that while some findings suggest possible cross-protection against BDBV, the evidence remains insufficient to determine clinically meaningful protection or quantify vaccine efficacy in humans. The guidance outlines the benefits, risks, and uncertainties of off-label use and recommends that the vaccine be used only within research protocols. It emphasizes the need for rapidly generating robust efficacy data through a ring randomized controlled trial, maintaining proven outbreak-control measures, and accelerating the development of BDBV-specific vaccines. The findings highlight the importance of further research to inform future policy decisions. The evidence is considered moderate in strength due to the lack of sufficient data on vaccine efficacy against BDBV. The guidance serves as a critical step in managing outbreaks while acknowledging the uncertainties surrounding the vaccine's effectiveness in this context.

The targets for five critical public health response indicators (case detection alerts, contact tracing, laboratory testing, isolation of infected persons, and safe and dignified burials) have not yet been met, and the outbreak continues to expand rapidly. What are the implications for public health practice? Substantial improvements in established outbreak control measures are crucial to rapidly detect and diagnose cases and isolate and provide treatment for infected persons, prevent funeral-associated transmission to prevent additional spread, and control this rapidly expanding outbreak. Altmetric: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) Ministry of Public Health declared an Ebola outbreak on May 15, 2026 (1). Two days later, CDC activated its Emergency Operations Center as part of the U.S. government response to this rapidly growing outbreak (2). This report describes the epidemiologic characteristics and monitoring of the ongoing outbreak in DRC. Investigation and Outcomes Background The 2026 Ebola DRC outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus is now the second largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded. As of August 21, 2026, DRC reported 5,458 confirmed cases and 2,606 (48%) confirmed deaths. Compared with previous Ebola outbreaks, the increase in cases in DRC is unprecedented, with approximately 5,000 cases in 100 days (Ebola Outbreak: Current Situation | CDC). Cases have been reported from six of the 26 DRC provinces (Bas-Uélé, Haut-Uélé, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, and Tshop), affecting 57 of 151 health zones in the affected provinces. Ituri province remains the outbreak epicenter, accounting for 84% of reported cases. Strategies known to control Ebola outbreaks include community-based surveillance, case detection alert notifications,* rapid and in-depth case investigations, identification and monitoring of contacts, infection control measures (e.g., prompt isolation of persons with suspected or confirmed Bundibugyo virus disease [BVD]), rapid diagnostic testing, mortality surveillance, and safe and dignified burials (SDBs).† Data Source Operational indicators for five domains have been generated based on experience with previous Ebola outbreaks, including DRC’s 2018 outbreak (3) (Table). Targets reflect the levels necessary to end the outbreak. The DRC Ministry of Public Health prepares publicly available daily situation reports, and CDC abstracts data from these reports to evaluate the established indicators each day. Indicator data are monitored over time to assess the outbreak trajectory. This activity was reviewed by CDC, deemed not research, and conducted consistent with applicable federal law and CDC policy.§ Operational Indicator Analysis Nearly all operational indicators remain below identified targets (Table). Operational indicator values were calculated for the 21-day period of July 31–August 21. The average percentage of alerts investigated within 24 hours (last reported August 5, 2026) was 83% (target = >90%). An average of 10.6 contacts were identified per confirmed case (target = ≥20), suggesting underreporting and underascertainment of case contacts. The percentage of confirmed new cases previously identified as known contacts (last reported July 12, 2026) was 15%–20% (target = >90%); this suggests that most cases are occurring outside known transmission chains. In addition, more than one half (59%) of confirmed Ebola deaths are occurring outside an Ebola treatment unit (ETU) (target = 0%), suggesting insufficient ETU capacity, fear of ETUs, and ongoing spread through unidentified transmission chains. Laboratory testing was performed for 72% of validated alerts (target = >90%), indicating that a substantial number of suspected cases remain untested. Test positivity was 24%, with a target of 0%. Although the national ETU bed occupancy was 64%, meeting the target of <80%, occupancy varied substantially by health zone, with some facilities unable to isolate all infected persons and reporting occupancies as high as 140%. Fewer than one half (49%) of affected health zones had at least one SDB team (target = 100%). Current data were not available for several response indicators, such as percentage of persons with confirmed BVD receiving prompt isolation (target = >90%) and percentage of deaths with SDBs (target = 100%), underscoring ongoing data gaps in this complex public health response. These missing data and operational gaps, together with continued geographic expansion of the outbreak, a high percentage of deaths occurring outside ETUs, and a low percentage of cases among persons previously identified as contacts, indicate uncontrolled expansion of the outbreak. Public health response activities are complicated by a protracted complex humanitarian emergency in the eastern part of DRC, including armed conflict, limited health infrastructure, population displacement and mobility, and constraints on access to affected communities. Containment and control of the 2026 Ebola disease outbreak requires integration and coordination of at least five response areas: 1) expansion of community-based surveillance systems ensuring rapid investigation of alerts; 2) improvements in contact tracing completeness and timeliness; 3) expansion of treatment and isolation capacity in affected health zones; 4) increased laboratory testing capacity, enabling prompt case identification; and 5) ensuring SDBs in affected health zones. In addition, collecting robust, high-quality data regarding these operational actions is essential at the health zone level; CDC’s continued support to the DRC Ministry of Public Health and partners with improving data collection is critical. Collecting data at the level of the health zone facilitates timely local outbreak response decisions. Rapidly enhancing international humanitarian coordination and mobilizing global technical, operational, and other needed support are critical for accelerating the response and controlling the outbreak. analysis.research_question_and_background: This study addresses the characteristics and monitoring of the 2026 Ebola disease outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, highlighting the need to understand the epidemiological patterns and response challenges of this emerging outbreak.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a retrospective analysis of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, focusing on six provinces and 57 health zones. It reports confirmed cases and deaths as of August 21, 2026, and evaluates the operational response measures across these regions.
analysis.methods: The study utilized surveillance data, laboratory testing results, and public health response metrics to assess the outbreak. It included the investigation of case detection alerts, contact tracing efforts, and the status of key operational indicators such as isolation capacity and safe burial practices.
analysis.main_results: As of August 21, 2026, the DRC reported 5,458 confirmed cases and 2,606 (48%) confirmed deaths. The outbreak was unprecedented, with approximately 5,000 cases in 100 days. Ituri province accounted for 84% of reported cases, and only 83% of alerts were investigated within 24 hours, falling short of the target of >90%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that the outbreak is not only extensive but also poorly controlled, with significant gaps in surveillance, contact tracing, and laboratory testing. The study highlights the need for improved operational response strategies to address these challenges.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results emphasize the importance of strengthening community-based surveillance systems, enhancing contact tracing, and improving laboratory testing capacity to effectively manage and contain the Bundibugyo virus outbreak and prevent further spread.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the availability of data for several response indicators, which were not reported. The evidence is based on surveillance and operational data, which may not fully capture the complexity of the outbreak, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study reports on the 2026 Bundibugyo virus Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, highlighting its unprecedented scale with 5,458 confirmed cases and 2,606 deaths as of August 21, 2026. Ituri province was the epicenter, accounting for 84% of cases. The study notes that most operational indicators, such as alert investigation and safe burial practices, were below target levels, indicating gaps in the public health response. These findings underscore the need for improved surveillance, contact tracing, and laboratory testing to manage the outbreak effectively. The evidence is based on reported data and operational metrics, which, while informative, have limitations due to incomplete information on key response indicators, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究探讨了刚果民主共和国由本迪布焦病毒引起的 2026 年埃博拉疾病 暴发 的特征和监测,强调需要了解这种新兴 暴发 的流行病学模式和应对挑战。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是对刚果民主共和国2026年本迪布焦病毒暴发的回顾性分析,重点关注6个省份和57个卫生区。它报告了截至 2026 年 8 月 21 日的确诊病例和死亡人数,并评估了这些地区的行动应对措施。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究利用 监测 数据、实验室测试结果和公共卫生响应指标来评估 暴发。它包括对病例检测警报、接触者追踪工作以及隔离能力和安全埋葬做法等关键运营指标的状态进行调查。
elements_zh.main_results: 截至 2026 年 8 月 21 日,刚果民主共和国报告了 5,458 例确诊病例和 2,606 例(48%)确诊死亡。暴发 是史无前例的,100 天内大约有 5,000 例病例。伊图里省占报告病例的 84%,只有 83% 的警报在 24 小时内得到调查,未达到 >90% 的目标。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,暴发 不仅范围广泛,而且控制不佳,在 监测、接触者追踪和实验室检测方面存在显着差距。该研究强调需要改进行动响应策略来应对这些挑战。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调了加强基于社区的 监测 系统、加强接触者追踪和提高实验室检测能力的重要性,以有效管理和遏制本迪布焦病毒 暴发 并防止进一步传播。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到若干反应指标数据可用性的限制,而这些指标尚未报告。该证据基于 监测 和操作数据,可能无法完全捕捉 暴发 的复杂性,从而导致置信度评估适中。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究探讨了刚果民主共和国由本迪布焦病毒引起的 2026 年埃博拉疾病 暴发 的特征和监测,强调需要了解这种新兴 暴发 的流行病学模式和应对挑战。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是对刚果民主共和国2026年本迪布焦病毒暴发的回顾性分析,重点关注6个省份和57个卫生区。它报告了截至 2026 年 8 月 21 日的确诊病例和死亡人数,并评估了这些地区的行动应对措施。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究利用 监测 数据、实验室测试结果和公共卫生响应指标来评估 暴发。它包括对病例检测警报、接触者追踪工作以及隔离能力和安全埋葬做法等关键运营指标的状态进行调查。
analysis_zh.main_results: 截至 2026 年 8 月 21 日,刚果民主共和国报告了 5,458 例确诊病例和 2,606 例(48%)确诊死亡。暴发 是史无前例的,100 天内大约有 5,000 例病例。伊图里省占报告病例的 84%,只有 83% 的警报在 24 小时内得到调查,未达到 >90% 的目标。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,暴发 不仅范围广泛,而且控制不佳,在 监测、接触者追踪和实验室检测方面存在显着差距。该研究强调需要改进行动响应策略来应对这些挑战。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调了加强基于社区的 监测 系统、加强接触者追踪和提高实验室检测能力的重要性,以有效管理和遏制本迪布焦病毒 暴发 并防止进一步传播。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到若干反应指标数据可用性的限制,而这些指标尚未报告。该证据基于 监测 和操作数据,可能无法完全捕捉 暴发 的复杂性,从而导致置信度评估适中。

papers.title: Bundibugyo at the Border: The 2026 Ebola Outbreak and the Case for Pre-emptive Countermeasure Equity.
papers.abstract: The 2026 Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda exposes a persistent structural flaw in global health security: preparedness remains overwhelmingly reactive and pathogen-specific. Despite the $518 million Africa CDC-WHO joint continental plan, no licensed BDBV vaccine or therapeutic is available; a 21-day (three-week) detection delay and cross-border transmission expose inadequate inter-epidemic investment in non-Zaire ebolavirus countermeasures. We argue for sustained, ring-fenced financing, institutionalised cross-border coordination, species-inclusive diagnostics, and real-time genomic data sharing to move African Ebola preparedness from reactive to pre-emptive.

papers.title: Aerosol-based disinfection protocol for aircraft: a solution for the conflict between material compatibility and antimicrobial efficacy.
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Every year, billions of passengers, pets, and livestock are transported by air, which increases the risk of a global spread of pathogens like severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 1 and 2, H1N1 influenza, the Ebola virus, and foot-and-mouth disease virus. However, due to its complexity and high safety standards, aircraft decontamination is limited to manual surface disinfection, and an approved method for disinfecting otherwise inaccessible areas is still unavailable. To address this issue, we present the development and validation of an effective room disinfection method utilizing low concentrations of aerosolized peroxyacetic acid (aPAA), stabilized by hydrogen peroxide, known as "dry fog." Therefore, we determined the minimal effective antimicrobial concentration of aPAA for a wide range of agents, including bacteria, viruses, and bacterial endospores. Then, we applied the developed disinfection protocol to a large panel of relevant materials multiple times in the context of the official material compatibility tests (MCTs) requested by the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) to demonstrate that its application will not cause a negative effect on the aircraft airworthiness. After successfully passing these complex material compatibility tests, we finally validated the disinfection protocol within a narrow-body aircraft A320 for its antimicrobial efficacy by using the most resistant microorganisms to aPAA among our test organisms, the bacteriophage MS2, and spores of Geobacillus stearothermophilus. Thus, we are now able to present the first aerosol-based room disinfection method suitable for aircraft that could easily be adopted for other aircraft types and other means of mass transport as well. IMPORTANCE: Despite numerous outbreaks in recent years, particularly the Ebola virus epidemic and the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 pandemic, there is still no approved method for disinfecting contaminated aircraft. Due to the highly complex nature of aircraft material and technology, it is difficult to balance the antimicrobial efficacy and material compatibility of the biocides used in a way that meets high safety standards. Here, we demonstrate an aerosol-based disinfection protocol using a mixture of peracetic acid and hydrogen peroxide. This protocol passed all material compatibility tests according to relevant aircraft certification specifications established by the European Union Aviation Safety Agency, as well as the manufacturer qualification test programs, and proved to be highly effective against viruses, bacteria, and even bacterial endospores without compromising the airworthiness of the aircraft. By targeting both contaminated surfaces and objects, as well as airborne pathogen reservoirs, it minimizes the spillover risk of zoonotic agents and prevents the mechanical transmission of high-consequence agricultural pathogens into disease-free geographical regions. This makes it the first suitable semi-automatic airborne disinfection method that can be used in addition to routine manual surface disinfection following contamination resulting from contact with people, animals, or goods infected or contaminated with high-consequence pathogens.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenge of disinfecting aircraft to prevent the global spread of pathogens like severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 1 and 2, H1N1 influenza, the Ebola virus, and foot-and-mouth disease virus.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study developed and validated an aerosol-based disinfection protocol using low concentrations of peroxyacetic acid (aPAA) stabilized by hydrogen peroxide, applied to a large panel of relevant materials in the context of official material compatibility tests (MCTs) requested by the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA).
analysis.methods: The methods involved demonstrating an aerosol-based disinfection protocol using a mixture of peracetic acid and hydrogen peroxide, and applying it to a wide range of agents, including bacteria, viruses, and bacterial endospores.
analysis.main_results: The protocol passed all material compatibility tests according to relevant aircraft certification specifications and proved to be highly effective against viruses, bacteria, and even bacterial endospores without compromising the airworthiness of the aircraft.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating the first aerosol-based room disinfection method suitable for aircraft, which could be adopted for other aircraft types and means of mass transport.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that this method could minimize the spillover risk of zoonotic agents and prevent the mechanical transmission of high-consequence agricultural pathogens into disease-free regions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is limited to abstract-only information, and the results are based on tests with the most resistant microorganisms to aPAA, which may not fully represent all potential pathogens.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents an aerosol-based disinfection protocol using peroxyacetic acid (aPAA) stabilized by hydrogen peroxide, known as 'dry fog,' to address the challenge of disinfecting aircraft. The protocol was developed to balance antimicrobial efficacy with material compatibility, passing all required tests for airworthiness. It was validated against the most resistant microorganisms, including bacteriophage MS2 and spores of Geobacillus stearothermophilus, demonstrating high effectiveness. The method could be adopted for other aircraft types and mass transport systems, reducing the risk of pathogen transmission. However, the evidence is based solely on abstract information, and the results may not fully represent all potential pathogens. The findings have implications for improving aircraft decontamination practices and preventing the spread of high-consequence pathogens.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决对飞机进行消毒的挑战,以防止严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 1 型和 2 型、H1N1 流感、埃博拉病毒 和口蹄疫病毒等病原体在全球传播。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究开发并验证了一种基于气溶胶的消毒方案,使用由过氧化氢稳定的低浓度过氧乙酸(aPAA),在欧盟航空安全局(EASA)要求的官方材料兼容性测试(MCT)的背景下应用于大量相关材料。
elements_zh.methods: 这些方法涉及展示使用过乙酸和过氧化氢混合物的基于气溶胶的消毒方案,并将其应用于多种介质,包括细菌、病毒和细菌内生孢子。
elements_zh.main_results: 该协议根据相关飞机审定规范通过了所有材料兼容性测试,并被证明对病毒、细菌甚至细菌内生孢子非常有效,且不影响飞机的适航性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这一发现解释为展示了第一种适用于飞机的基于气溶胶的房间消毒方法,该方法可用于其他飞机类型和大众运输工具。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,这种方法可以最大限度地减少人畜共患病原体的 跨物种溢出 风险,并防止高后果农业病原体机械 传播 进入无病区。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据仅限于抽象信息,结果基于对 aPAA 耐药性最强的微生物进行的测试,这可能无法完全代表所有潜在的病原体。

papers.abstract_zh: 无标题:每年,数十亿名乘客、宠物和牲畜通过航空运输,这增加了严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒1型和2型、H1N1流感、埃博拉病毒及口蹄疫病毒等病原体在全球传播的风险。然而,由于飞机消毒过程复杂且安全标准极高,现有消毒方法仅限于人工表面消毒,而针对无法触及区域的批准消毒方法仍然缺失。为解决此问题,本研究开发并验证了一种有效的机舱消毒方法,该方法利用低浓度气溶胶化过氧乙酸(aPAA,由过氧化氢稳定)实现“干雾”消毒。因此,我们确定了aPAA对广泛病原体(包括细菌、病毒及细菌芽孢)的最低有效抗菌浓度。随后,在欧洲航空安全局(EASA)要求的官方材料兼容性测试(MCTs)背景下,我们在大量相关材料上多次应用所开发的消毒方案,以证明其应用不会对飞机适航性产生负面影响。在成功通过这些复杂的材料兼容性测试后,我们最终在空客A320窄体飞机内验证了该消毒方案的抗菌效果,所用测试微生物为对aPAA最具抵抗力的病毒之一——MS2噬菌体及嗜热脂肪芽孢杆菌(Geobacillus stearothermophilus)芽孢。因此,我们现已能够首次提出一种适用于飞机的气溶胶室内消毒方法,该方法可轻松推广至其他机型及其他大规模运输工具。重要性:尽管近年来出现了多次暴发,特别是埃博拉病毒疫情及严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2型大流行,但目前仍无批准用于污染飞机的消毒方法。由于飞机材料与技术高度复杂,难以在抗菌效果与消毒剂材料兼容性之间实现平衡,以满足高安全标准。本研究展示了一种基于过氧乙酸与过氧化氢混合物的气溶胶消毒方案。该方案通过了欧洲航空安全局制定的相关飞机认证规范及制造商资格测试项目的所有材料兼容性测试,证明对病毒、细菌甚至细菌芽孢均高度有效,且不会损害飞机适航性。通过同时靶向污染表面、物体及空气中的病原体储存宿主,该方案最大限度降低了人兽共患病病原体的跨物种溢出风险,并防止高后果农业病原体通过机械传播传入无疫地区。这使其成为首个可用于补充常规人工表面消毒的半自动空气消毒方法,适用于因接触感染或污染人、动物或物品而导致的污染情况。
